items.stem: Complete the statement: Contribution per unit is …
options: selling price − total cost per unit
selling price per unit − variable cost per unit
items.answer: selling price per unit − variable cost per unit
items.markingKey: selling price per unit − variable cost per unit. Contributes to fixed costs and profit [1]

items.stem: Explain what is meant by contribution.
items.answer: Contribution is selling price less variable costs; it is the amount each unit contributes first to covering fixed costs and then to profit.
items.markingKey: SP − VC [1]; covers fixed costs then profit [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why fixed costs are not included in the contribution per unit.
items.answer: They do not change with output in the short run, so they are not affected by producing one more unit; spreading them per unit would give misleading decisions.
items.markingKey: Do not vary with output [1]; misleading per unit [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the margin of safety is useful to managers.
items.answer: It shows how far sales could fall before a loss is made, indicating the level of risk.
items.markingKey: Fall in sales before loss [1]; risk [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the effect on the break-even point of an increase in the selling price.
items.answer: Contribution per unit rises, so fewer units are needed to cover fixed costs; break-even falls.

items.markingKey: the total revenue line crosses the total cost line. Revenue = total cost [1]

items.stem: State three assumptions of break-even analysis.
items.answer: Selling price and variable cost per unit are constant; fixed costs are fixed; all output is sold; single product or constant sales mix.

items.stem: Explain how a break-even chart can help a business plan.
items.answer: It shows visually the profit or loss at any output, the break-even point and margin of safety, and the effect of changes in price or costs.
items.markingKey: Visual profit/loss at outputs [1]; what-if changes [1] [2]
